Subject: Encryption choices & audit artifacts — next actions for FinCo pilot

Hi Alyssa / Samir — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track asks from the discovery: 

Summary of what we covered
- Use case: low-latency inference for customer-facing fraud models; some inputs will be PII (PII flagging in ingest).
- Compliance driver: FinCo needs cryptographic controls that allow 'customer-controlled keys' and long-lived audit retention for forensics.

High-level encryption options (what we can offer)
1) Hosted (fastest onboarding) — Redwood-managed keys (AES-256 at rest), TLS 1.2+ in transit. Suitable when customer cannot host KMS; we provide SOC2 artifacts.
2) BYOK via cloud KMS (recommended middle path) — Redwood integrates with customer KMS (cross-account AWS KMS or equivalent). Keys remain in customer account; Redwood encrypts at rest using CMKs that we cannot directly export.
3) Private deployment + HSM (maximum control) — customer runs Private stack (VPC/on-prem) or we deploy into customer-controlled network; HSM-backed keys with customer-held key material possible depending on deployment.

Specific asks you mentioned and proposed owner for follow-up
- Requirement: keys must be in customer's AWS account (FinCo) and we should be able to encrypt/decrypt without Redwood holding plaintext key material. (Alyssa) — Action: confirm whether cross-account decrypt in-hosting model is acceptable.
- Logging: request per-request telemetry for audit (redacted payloads), retention 7 years. (Samir) — Action: provide logging retention and redaction options.
- Evidence: SOC2 report, KMS integration examples, key rotation policy. (Legal/Compliance) — Action: attach checklist.

Immediate next steps (proposed)
- I attached a 1-pager (BYOK-options-summary.pdf) with the three architectural patterns and what changes for telemetry and footprint.
- Can we do a technical deep-dive with your infra/security team next week? I can bring Ben (crypto lead) and Soojin (solutions engineer). Suggested slots: Tue 3/23 10–11am PT or Wed 3/24 9–10am PT.
- Please confirm the KMS provider (AWS/GCP/Azure) and whether FinCo requires HSM-backed key material.

Thanks — I’ll add a short runbook and sample IAM role snippet once you confirm cloud provider.

Connor O'Brien

Connor — thanks for the clear recap. A couple clarifications from FinCo Security/Legal: 

- Preferred KMS: AWS KMS with CloudHSM-backed keys. Key material must be created in our AWS account and should not be exportable by vendor services.
- Telemetry & logging: we need per-request metadata (request id, model id, timestamp, redacted input hash) retained for 7 years in a read-only audit store. Full plaintext request bodies should never leave FinCo enclave unless explicitly redacted/consented.
- Evidence: SOC2 + encryption configuration screenshots or runbook that shows how keys are configured, rotation schedule, and access controls.

Questions: 
1) Can Redwood integrate with our cross-account AWS KMS setup so the CMK is in our account and Redwood performs crypto operations without Redwood ever being able to retrieve raw key material?
2) For hosted offering, what telemetry can be provided without exposing PII? Will Redwood push logs into our read-only bucket or do we pull?

We are aiming to finalize architecture for pilot by 3/31. If you can have a technical runbook and sample IAM trust policy ahead of the deep-dive that will help.

Best,
Alyssa Morgan
Head of Security | FinCo
alyssa.morgan@finco.com

Alyssa — great questions. Short answers here and then propose a runbook deliverable we can share before the call.

1) AWS KMS / CloudHSM — what we can support
- Dedicated & Private deployments: we can perform cryptographic operations against a CMK located in your AWS account via cross-account grants/roles. The CMK never leaves your account; Redwood does not import raw key material. This satisfies non-export requirement.
- Hosted: we do not currently import customer key material into our hosted multi-tenant control plane. We can, however, integrate via a TLS+Mutual-Auth gateway to call into customer KMS endpoints for some patterns but that requires Private or Dedicated connectivity for production SLAs.

2) Telemetry and logging options
- We can stream redacted per-request metadata (request id, model id, latency, token counts, redacted input hash) into a customer-owned S3/GCS bucket with role-based read-only ACLs. Payload-level PII is never written to logs unless you explicitly opt-in for debugging.
- Retention: default 90/365/1095 days; we support custom retention policies (we can configure lifecycle rules on the audit bucket to meet 7-year retention). Note: long retention has cost and e-discovery implications — we'll coordinate with FinCo legal.

Attached: BYOK-options-summary.pdf (one-pager) and a draft sample IAM trust snippet (inline below).

Proposed pre-call deliverables (we will share by Tue 3/23 EOD):
- Short runbook: KMS integration patterns + sample cross-account role policy
- SOC2 artifact pack index (redacted screenshots, control mappings) — Soojin to assemble
- Logging runbook: how logs are redacted, where they land, lifecycle rules — Ben to draft

Would you prefer Tue 3/23 10am PT or Wed 3/24 9am PT for the deep-dive? I can pencil both but will confirm once you pick one.

Connor
